sessionTitle: Modern resiliency from build to recovery through Agentic AI

announcements.name: Public preview of Azure Infrastructure Resiliency Manager
announcements.shortDescription: Lets customers manage zonal resiliency through application-level goals, Advisor-powered recommendations, resiliency drills, and recovery plans
announcements.longDescription: Azure Infrastructure Resiliency Manager entered public preview, allowing customers to manage zonal resiliency at an application level rather than per individual resource, using service groups. It introduces goals for setting resiliency targets, recommendations powered by Advisor, resiliency drills to simulate failures (powered by Chaos Studio), and recovery plans to orchestrate failover. The experience can be managed through Azure Portal, PowerShell CLI, and Azure Copilot, with intelligent guidance brought into developer workflows including GitHub Copilot.

announcements.name: Resiliency drills powered by Chaos Studio
announcements.shortDescription: Simulate failures such as an availability-zone outage to test an application's resiliency posture
announcements.longDescription: Resiliency drills let customers test configured resiliency by simulating real-life failure scenarios, such as a particular availability zone going down. Powered by Chaos Studio, the drills help simulate and test an application's resiliency posture before an actual outage occurs. The capability is part of the Azure Infrastructure Resiliency Manager public preview.

announcements.name: Recovery plans
announcements.shortDescription: Define an ordered workflow capturing interdependencies for failing over resources like databases and VMs during an actual outage
announcements.longDescription: Recovery plans address the challenge of failing over the many interdependent resources in an application during an actual outage, such as failing over a database and a VM in the correct order. They allow customers to create a workflow defining the order in which various resources need to be recovered. The capability is available in public preview as part of the Azure Infrastructure Resiliency Manager.

announcements.name: Azure Advisor AI-powered prioritization experience enters limited preview
announcements.shortDescription: Collapses hundreds of recommendations into a top-five prioritized, exportable action plan ranked by blast radius, criticality, deadlines, and cost; sign-ups offered after the session
announcements.longDescription: Azure Advisor's AI-powered prioritization experience collapses hundreds of recommendations down to a top-five list with an action plan specific to the customer's environment. Microsoft plans to refine the experience further and bring the resiliency flows and advisor flows closer together for seamless end-to-end resiliency management. The experience started limited preview the day of the session, with a few sign-up spots available by meeting the presenters after the session.

announcements.name: AI-powered resource-level prioritization (landing soon)
announcements.shortDescription: Will rank individual resources within a recommendation using live signals such as active service health events and prod/non-prod distinctions
announcements.longDescription: Landing soon, AI-powered resource-level prioritization will take Advisor's prioritization a step further by ranking which specific resources within a recommendation to fix first, since applications typically have hundreds of resources. It incorporates live signals from the environment, such as whether a resource is impacted by an active service health event or whether it is a production versus non-production instance, alongside an application's HA goal. This means customers will know not only which issue types to prioritize but also exactly which resources within those types to start with.

announcements.name: Chaos Studio Workspaces public preview on June 11
announcements.shortDescription: An application-centric reimagining with new scenarios and a new agentic service for rehearsing feared outages
announcements.longDescription: Azure Chaos Studio Workspaces supports the "stay resilient" phase by validating that an application's resilience matches expectations, since customers often believe they are resilient until an availability zone goes down, an AI workload silently degrades, or throttling cascades. Announced at Build, Chaos Studio Workspaces launches in public preview [inferred] on June 11 as a complete reimagining of the experience with application-centric workspaces, new scenarios, and a new agentic service. It enables customers to rehearse the outages they actually fear.
